note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
David asks, “What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.” Paul tells us who that son of man is. He quotes David, “But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels”, and then names him: “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.”

The so-called yaya israelites say the foolish thing that Jesus was an idol not prophesied in the Old Testament. But David is writing about a son of man made lower than the angels; that son of man is Jesus Christ, the black messiah.

Christ had to be made lower than the angels so that he could die. In his angelic form he would be immortal; he had to come after the seed of Abraham, David and Joseph, from sperm, so that he could taste death for every Israelite man. “For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.” He is the captain of our salvation, made perfect through sufferings.

“For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.” The dominion David speaks of, all things under his feet, is Christ's, though we do not yet see it all.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
David says of the son of man, “thou hast put all things under his feet”. Paul shows how that came to be. “But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept. For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.” Christ was made lower than the angels so he could die, and he rose as the firstfruits.

“But every man in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; afterward they that are Christ’s at his coming. Then cometh the end, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have put down all rule and all authority and power. For he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet. The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.”

“For he hath put all things under his feet.” God has put all things under Christ's feet, subjecting the whole earth and the spiritual realm to the Son. That is the dominion David saw, the son of man crowned with glory and honour. “But when he saith all things are put under him, it is manifest that he is excepted, which did put all things under him”: the Father who put all things under Christ is not himself under him.

precepts.text: When all is subdued to Christ, the Son himself will be subject to the Father, that God may be all in all.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
All things are put under the feet of the son of man, but Paul shows where it ends: “And when all things shall be subdued unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subject unto him that put all things under him, that God may be all in all.”

When all is subdued to Christ, the Son himself will be subject unto the Father, that God may be all in all. The dominion given to the son of man in Psalm 8 is real dominion over the works of God's hands, but the Father stands above the Son, and the kingdom is handed back to him.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
Christ said it himself: “Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I.”

The Father is greater than the Son. That is why, after all is subdued under his feet, Christ hands the kingdom to the Father. He is the son of man made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory and honour, given dominion over the works of God's hands, yet the one who gave him that dominion is greater than he.

note.label: Psalm 8: The Son of Man Made a Little Lower Than the Angels

precepts.why:
Christ said the Father is greater than he, yet he was a god on earth. After he healed the man at the pool, “Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said unto him, Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The man told the Jews it was Jesus, “And therefore did the Jews persecute Jesus, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day.”

“But Jesus answered them, My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. Therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only had broken the sabbath, but said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God.”

The Jews sought to kill Jesus for making himself equal with God. He was a god on earth, the son of man crowned with glory and honour with all things under his feet, and still he said the Father is greater than I. Both are true: he is the Son with dominion, and the Father is above him.

points: He ordained strength out of the mouth of babes because of the enemies: it takes the oppression and the affliction to raise these youth up.
The enemies are Esau and the other nations; the avengers are God's prophets, and the babes are the ones in these seats who can explain it.
The Most High's name is excellent in all the earth, and he set his glory above the heavens because he dwells in the third heaven.

points: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings he has ordained strength. This is why you see young men and young women rising up to teach the bible and change their lives. And "young" is relative: our ancestors lived to 900, Abraham had Isaac at 100 and Sarah at 90, so at 60 or 70 you are young, and we are all young in spirit.
